reason: Changes only the writer, while the reader still parses a fixed number of header lines, causing round-trip tests to fail; this is a partial fix (S1).

Copies the example transformation without adding the topocentric frame location attribute, so tests fail during construction; this reflects incomplete understanding of the coordinate-frame framework (P1).
Failure occurs during test import because a dependency deprecation warning is treated as an error, independently of the patch; this should be an environment/test-framework problem (OTHER-V5).
Only adds an import-path fallback for ordinary fields, while the test targets another serialization entry point for nested classes; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).

Fixes the return value used for field reconstruction but defers evaluation and validation of the storage object until access, changing initialization timing; this is an execution-timing mismatch (V4).
Fixes equality and hashing, but uses the object address to break ordering ties when counters are equal, so stable ordering is not guaranteed; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).
Only changes the utility function, while the template-filter entry point still requires an id argument, omitting a corresponding entry-point change; this is incomplete scope (L1).
Insists on converting standard-library escaping back to the old entities to accommodate old tests, although the issue accepts the new output; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).
Returns the lazy format argument unchanged instead of converting it to a string before parsing, causing the lazy-format test to fail; this is a partial fix (S1).
Forwards the startup option as two arguments, while the test requires a combined argument. Forwarding is implemented and the failure is in the argument representation (V2).
Still filters each search term separately instead of combining conditions, leaving the join-count problem unresolved; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).
Changes the wrong layer: it fixes a form field although the problem occurs in the model-save path. This should be misinterpretation of the target and architectural layer (P1).
Only expands the handling of type errors and omits value errors from similar invalid inputs; this should be a partial fix (S1).

The issue requests dictionary-style query results only, and the patch preserves the existing type of list-style results. The tests additionally require those results to become dictionaries too; this is an additional test requirement (V1).
A batch edit fails partway through and leaves an incomplete line that prevents module import. The model then submits as if the state were undamaged; this is a tool failure/state misjudgment (I1).
Only transcodes the Message-ID locally; the Unicode hostname remains in the global cache and later sending fails. This is a regression (V3).
The local variable is unassigned on a cache hit, so repeated hostname lookup raises an exception; the change breaks the existing cache path (V3).

Only detects asynchronous capability downstream in exception handling and does not add the missing initialization call during middleware construction; this is an incorrect intervention layer or incomplete scope (L1).

Preserves a tuple special case for backward compatibility, so a single two-element tuple child is still reconstructed as keyword arguments, while the test requires uniform positional arguments; this is a representation mismatch (V2).
Writes the attribute value as a string instead of an integer. Rendering is identical, but the type read by the test differs; this is a representation mismatch (V2).
Merges the attributes only during rendering instead of storing them during form initialization, so a test that reads them before rendering fails; this is an execution-timing mismatch (V4).
Implements some configurable error-code behavior but does not update constraint equality and output representations, so target tests still fail; this should be a partial fix (S1).
Implements the target feature, but mismatched formatting arguments break the existing representation output; this should be a regression (V3).
Implements the target feature, but the field-based uniqueness path overrides the existing error code and breaks established validation behavior; this should be a regression (V3).

The archived patch differs from the model final submission and has corrupted context-line encoding. The evaluation outcome cannot be attributed to model behavior; this should be an archival/evaluation problem (OTHER).
The intended constructor-signature change is absent from the final patch, causing constraint construction to fail immediately; this should be an unapplied edit/state misjudgment (I1).

The patch retains only a temporary reproduction script and makes no production-code change. The model mistakes an existing earlier fix for the target work; this should be problem misinterpretation (P1).
Only clones the query object without adding the columns required for ordering to the result, leaving the target behavior unimplemented; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).

Follows the issue suggestion to unpack a function with preset arguments during initialization, losing the function object and its binding structure and failing to produce the tested representation; this is distraction by a suggestion (P2).
Fixes collation propagation on only some paths and still omits other scenarios that create or alter foreign-key columns; this is a partial fix (S1).
Only excludes the primary-key constraint; the field-level unique constraint and the combined unique constraint still produce two constraints with the same name. This is a partial fix (S1).
Sets Content-Length to 0 for a HEAD response although the GET body is nonempty. The protocol only permits the GET length here; this reflects misinterpretation of a domain rule (P1).
The patch makes HEAD bodyless and gives it the same Content-Length as GET, satisfying the protocol. The test additionally forbids that header; this should be an additional test requirement (V1).
Copies the axes-setting approach when fixing the parent check, so the subfigure legend still refers to the root figure; this reflects misinterpretation of a domain rule (P1).
Only fixes alignment in the horizontal packer, while the vertical packer still uses the same old logic; this is a partial fix (S1).
Only sets figure-object state and continues computing with a null renderer, so the target layout test fails; this is a partial fix (S1).

Only removes the draggable helper from object state instead of making shared callbacks serializable, so the canvas is still written to the serialized stream; this is an incorrect intervention layer or incomplete scope (L1).

Only braces colons and does not handle spaces. The model treats ordinary spaces as requiring no escape and misses the requirement to represent them as `\\;`; this reflects a narrowed interpretation of math-escaping rules (P1).

Only handles spaces and does not brace colons. The model narrows the issue to space spacing and misses the requirement to represent colons as `{:}`; this reflects a narrowed interpretation of math-escaping rules (P1).
Replaces the entire math wrapper with plain-text output, losing the existing mathdefault wrapper and failing to produce the target format; this should be an incorrect strategy (S2).
Follows a source-code hint comment to add Collection limit recalculation, while the actual requirement is shared units on twin axes. The direction is diverted; this is distraction by a hint (P2).
Does not set units on the twin axes and only preserves data limits, leaving the tested requirement that both axes have the same units unimplemented; this should be a partial fix (S1).
Only handles byte data in the request body and omits string conversion for URL parameters, so another call path fails; this is a partial fix (S1).

Protects commas inside parentheses and character classes as well as quantifier braces, exceeding the rule that only quantifier braces are protected; an invalid-regex case raises no error. This reflects rule misinterpretation (P1).
The comma-separated escaping change consumes backslashes and breaks previously valid regular expressions; this is a regression (V3).
Still uses comma-based splitting, so commas in quantifiers remain delimiters and even the issue examples fail; this reflects problem misinterpretation (P1).

Failure occurs during test import because a required dependency is not installed, causing collection errors independently of patch logic; this should be an environment/test-framework problem (OTHER-V5).
The insertion command returns success but does not change the file. The model proceeds as if the edit were applied and ultimately omits the key repair; this is a tool failure/state misjudgment (I1).
An editing script accidentally deletes most of the target class implementation, causing test collection to fail without the model noticing; this is a tool failure/state misjudgment (I1).
Follows the tentative clipping suggestion in the issue and retains a finite first threshold, while the test requires positive infinity; the direction is diverted by a suggestion (P2).
Fixes dedent handling but makes prepend/append content inherit body indentation, changing the established verbatim insertion behavior; this is a regression (V3).
Only switches return-annotation rendering instead of using the property-signature path that can create cross-references, so the target nodes are not generated; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).
The output structure for a multi-argument signature differs from the per-argument pairing format required by the test; this is an output-representation mismatch (V2).

Only adds inherited attributes during documentation lookup/filtering and does not change member discovery, so instance attributes defined in the base-class initializer still do not appear; this is a partial fix (S1).
The source-read event now covers parsed includes, but the same change also transforms literal-include content and breaks existing behavior; this is a regression (V3).
Implements include-content replacement; the only failure is an extra trailing newline in event text. This should be an output-representation mismatch (V2).
Collects multiple signatures but retains a continuation backslash on the first line or omits an arrow, so the output string differs from the assertion; this is an output-representation mismatch (V2).
Fixes parentheses in Max/Min output but replaces the existing printer entry point and breaks established behavior such as list printing; this is a regression (V3).
Calls the solver and returns its result, but squaring transforms the equation and loses equivalence with the original equation; this is an incorrect strategy (S2).
Only adds a fallback for equalities, but failure occurs in another equality assertion; adding inequality support would not make it pass. This should be an incorrect strategy (S2).
Replaces an exception with a returned ConditionSet and changes test assertions, breaking the existing caller contract; this is a regression (V3).
Only fixes the zero-block type in block-matrix multiplication and does not change matrix-addition construction, so another zero-matrix addition test still fails; this is a partial fix (S1).
The subclassing change is mostly correct, but some constructor paths still return the base class, degrading subclass objects in scenarios such as resizing; this should be a partial fix (S1).

Recognizes that operation paths still return the base class but deliberately narrows the requirement to constructors only, leaving operation results outside the subclass; this reflects incomplete problem understanding (P1).
Reverses the argument order of an established interface and loses a default value, producing the wrong Josephus-permutation size; this reflects misinterpretation of a domain rule (P1).
Obtains the wrong object type inside a classmethod, so the constructor cannot be found and an error is raised; this reflects misinterpretation of a domain rule (P1).
